content: Nitroglycerin ointment is a medication prescribed to prevent chest pain, also known as angina. It achieves this by relaxing the blood vessels in the heart, which increases the supply of blood and oxygen to the heart muscle. While its primary use is for angina, it may also be prescribed for other conditions. If you have questions about its use for other purposes, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Nitroglycerin ointment is applied to the skin and is typically used three to six times daily. Your doctor may instruct you to remove the ointment at a specific time each day. It is crucial to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully. If you have any doubts or questions, ask your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Use the ointment exactly as prescribed, without applying more or less than directed or using it more frequently than instructed. This medication helps control chest pain but does not cure the underlying condition. Continue using it even if you feel well, and do not stop using it without consulting your doctor, as abrupt discontinuation may lead to chest pain. Use the paper to spread the ointment in a thin layer over a relatively hair-free area of skin, such as the chest, ensuring the area is at least 2 inches by 3 inches. Do not rub the ointment into the skin. Leave the paper on top of the ointment and secure it in place using an elastic bandage, hosiery, or tape. After application, wash your hands thoroughly to avoid getting the ointment on your fingers. Over time, nitroglycerin may lose its effectiveness due to tolerance. If your angina symptoms worsen, such as more frequent, prolonged, or severe attacks, contact your doctor immediately. In addition to angina, nitroglycerin ointment may be used to improve blood circulation in patients with Raynaud's disease. Discuss the potential risks and benefits of using this medication for your condition with your doctor. Before using nitroglycerin ointment, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to nitroglycerin in any form (ointment, tablets, or patches), isosorbide, or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, including aspirin, beta blockers (e.g., atenolol, metoprolol, propranolol), calcium channel blockers (e.g., amlodipine, diltiazem, verapamil), dihydroergotamine, sildenafil, and any vitamins or supplements. Notify your doctor if you have a history of anemia, glaucoma, or recent head trauma. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while using this medication, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are using nitroglycerin ointment. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness or dizziness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Ask your doctor about the safe consumption of alcohol while using this medication, as alcohol can exacerbate its side effects. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Common side effects of nitroglycerin ointment include headaches, skin irritation or rash, dizziness, upset stomach, and flushing (a sensation of warmth). These side effects are usually mild, but if they persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Severe side effects, such as blurred vision, dry mouth, chest pain, or fainting, require immediate medical attention. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store nitroglycerin ointment out of reach of children and away from other ointments or creams. Keep the tube tightly closed after each use and store it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and any recommended laboratory tests. Note that nitroglycerin ointment is not intended for use during acute angina attacks. Continue using nitroglycerin tablets or spray for immediate relief of chest pain. If you experience persistent headaches, consult your doctor about taking acetaminophen. Do not take aspirin or other headache medications without your doctor’s approval. If skin irritation occurs, try applying the ointment to a different area of skin. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. The brand name for nitroglycerin ointment is Nitro-Bid®.
